source_read: Texts of PMC3844112, PMC12502574 and PMC9926328 saved in the blind round (scratchpad/bd-dd/s271/); browser not reopened.

results.corrected_extracted: At least 11 questionnaires measured strategy use (PBSS, NCHA, CAS, PSQ, PBSM, SQ, SCQ and four unnamed), most in several versions differing in items, response scale and time window; the PBSS was the most used (36 studies, about 58%, by the text; its time-window subtotals (24 + 5 + 4) and Table 1 reach 33, its response-scale subtotals with the 4 yes/no studies 35).
results.corrected_locator: Measurement of PBS, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs; Table 1; Measurement of PBS › Variants of the PBSS, 1st paragraph
results.note: Only the time-window subtotals reach 33; scale subtotals are 16 + 15 + 4 yes/no = 35. Versions differing in items, scale and window: 3rd paragraph. 36/62 = 58.1%. Role fits.
13/62 = 21.0%; the 13 include studies with only one or two avoidance items. The Conclusion recommends excluding avoidance strategies; narrow definition: before, during and/or after drinking.
As printed: 2351 - 1048 = 1303 screened; 88 full texts; 39 + 14 = 53 excluded; 35 included; rerun added 7. The 2351 equals the July 2025 rerun totals, not the abstract's first-search counts (1850).

Recounted from all 35 rows: 17, 9, 4, 4 (one a rapid review), 1; no trial. Quantitative also covers brief reports and unlabelled rows. The 28-sum breakdown (20/1/4/2/1) is in Results, 3rd paragraph: add to locator.

results.corrected_extracted: A 'no benzodiazepine' formulary policy in six Kentucky outpatient mental health clinics (2016) was followed by an 89% fall in benzodiazepine prescriptions over two years; the Discussion says that approaches enforcing cessation as non-negotiable may differ from core harm-reduction principles.
results.corrected_locator: Results › Policy › Prescribing, 1st paragraph; Appendix 1, Table 1 (Agrawal et al.); Discussion › Limitations in current prescribing practices, 1st paragraph
results.note: Kentucky appears only in Table 1 (Agrawal row). The Discussion hedges ('may differ'), so 'departs' overstates slightly. Six clinics, 2016 and 89% over two years confirmed; 'followed by' rightly avoids causal wording.
Results, 1st paragraph (88 full texts, 35 included) and Methods › Search strategy, 1st paragraph (14 February to 30 March 2024; rerun 7 July 2025) as printed.

Table 1 rows match: forum N = 122 (qualitative), Speed et al. 45 (qualitative), Kerr et al. 252 (cross-sectional survey; avoiding injecting alone is one of four requirements). The forum's dose and frequency details are rightly left out.

Results, 3rd paragraph: no significant effect of time in the placebo-brownie session on any pharmacodynamic outcome; the abstract says the same. The Table's placebo peak changes (for example liking 23.8) are descriptive only.
